STEP 01 - Objective¶

The objective of this assignment is to develop a Hybrid Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) system by integrating Deep Neural Networks with Hidden Markov Models.

The implemented system performs:

  • Speech preprocessing
  • MFCC feature extraction
  • Log-Mel Spectrogram extraction
  • DNN/LSTM based acoustic modeling
  • HMM based temporal sequence modeling
  • Viterbi decoding
  • Word Error Rate (WER) evaluation

Dataset¶

Dataset Used: LibriSpeech ASR Corpus

Subset: test-clean

The dataset consists of speech audio samples along with corresponding text transcriptions.

## STEP 9.2 Define LSTM Acoustic Model
import torch.nn as nn
class AcousticModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(
    self,
    input_dim,
    hidden_dim,
    output_dim
    ):
        super(
        AcousticModel,
        self
        ).__init__()
        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(
        input_dim,
        hidden_dim,
        batch_first=True
        )
        self.fc = nn.Linear(
        hidden_dim,
        output_dim
        )
    def forward(
    self,
    x
    ):
        lstm_output, _ = self.lstm(x)
        output = self.fc(
        lstm_output
        )
        return output

criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(
model.parameters(),
lr=0.001
)

for epoch in range(epochs):
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    outputs = model(X)
    loss = criterion(
    outputs.reshape(-1, num_states),
    y.reshape(-1)
    )
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    print(
    f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{epochs}, Loss={loss.item():.4f}"
    )

## STEP 10.2 - Create HMM Transition Matrix
transition_matrix = torch.zeros(
num_states,
num_states
)
for i in range(num_states):
    # stay in same state
    transition_matrix[i][i] = 0.6
    # move to next state
    if i + 1 < num_states:
        transition_matrix[i][i+1] = 0.4
    else:
        transition_matrix[i][i] = 1.0

## STEP 10.3 Implement Viterbi Algorithm
def viterbi_decode(
emissions,
transitions
):
    time_steps, states = emissions.shape
    dp = torch.zeros(
    time_steps,
    states
    )
    backpointer = torch.zeros(
    time_steps,
    states,
    dtype=torch.long
    )
    dp[0] = torch.log(
    emissions[0] + 1e-10
    )
    for t in range(
    1,
    time_steps
    ):
        for s in range(states):
            probabilities = (
            dp[t-1]
            +
            torch.log(
            transitions[:,s] + 1e-10
            )
            )
            best_previous = torch.argmax(
            probabilities
            )
            dp[t][s] = (
            probabilities[best_previous]
            +
            torch.log(
            emissions[t][s] + 1e-10
            )
            )
            backpointer[t][s] = best_previous
    # Backtracking
    best_path = []
    last_state = torch.argmax(
    dp[-1]
    )
    best_path.append(
    last_state.item()
    )
    for t in range(
    time_steps-1,
    0,
    -1
    ):
        last_state = backpointer[t][last_state]
        best_path.append(
            last_state.item()
        )
    best_path.reverse()
    return best_path

## STEP 11.2 - Convert HMM States to Text
recognized_words = []
previous_state = None
for state in decoded_states:
    # avoid repeated states
    if state != previous_state:
        recognized_words.append(
    state_word_map[state]
    )
    previous_state = state
recognized_text = " ".join(
recognized_words
)
print("Actual Transcript:")
print(transcript)
print("\nRecognized Text:")
print(recognized_text)

Conclusion¶

A Hybrid HMM-DNN based Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) system was successfully designed and implemented using the LibriSpeech dataset.

The implementation demonstrated the complete speech recognition pipeline from raw audio processing to final text evaluation.

Key Components Implemented¶

1. Speech Preprocessing¶

The speech waveform was processed using:

  • Signal normalization
  • Speech framing
  • Hamming windowing

These steps converted continuous speech signals into suitable short-time speech frames for acoustic analysis.

2. Acoustic Feature Extraction¶

Two important acoustic representations were extracted:

  • MFCC (Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients)
  • Log-Mel Spectrogram features

MFCC features were used as the primary input representation for acoustic modelling.

3. DNN Acoustic Model¶

A Deep Neural Network based acoustic model was developed using an LSTM architecture.

The LSTM model captured sequential speech information and generated acoustic state probability distributions.

4. HMM State Modelling¶

The DNN generated probabilities were integrated with Hidden Markov Model based temporal modelling.

The HMM transition matrix represented state movements across speech frames.

5. Viterbi Decoding¶

The Viterbi algorithm was implemented to identify the optimal hidden acoustic state sequence.

This demonstrated the decoding process used in hybrid speech recognition systems.

6. Performance Evaluation¶

The ASR system performance was evaluated using:

  • Word Error Rate (WER)
  • Recognition Accuracy

The results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining neural acoustic models with probabilistic sequence modelling.

Final Outcome¶

The assignment successfully demonstrates:

Speech Signal
→ Feature Extraction
→ LSTM Acoustic Model
→ HMM Integration
→ Viterbi Decoding
→ Recognized Text Evaluation

This Hybrid HMM-DNN approach combines the representation learning capability of deep neural networks with the sequential modelling strength of Hidden Markov Models.
